The Western Disturbance now seen as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level with the trough aloft in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along long 67°E to the north of Lat 30°N.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over East Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood and extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The trough now runs from the above cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood to Northwest Bay of Bengalacross Jharkhand, Gangetic West Bengal and Odisha at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal & Sikkim & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over central Assam & neighbourhood persists and now seen at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Arabian Sea & adjoining Lakshadweep area at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Gulf of Mannar & neighbourhood persist and now seen at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
A Low Pressure Area is likely to form over Southeast Bay of Bengal around 13th November, 2026. It is likely to move northwestwards and become well marked low pressure area during subsequent 24 hours.
